verdict.label: Full review
verdict.summary: Registering a multitenant app takes minutes, but users in other organizations often can't consent until you're a verified publisher (Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program) or their admin grants consent.

composioFit.summary: Composio does not provide a managed OAuth app for Microsoft Entra ID, so you must bring your own OAuth app and configure the redirect URI from your Composio auth config.
whyOwnApp: Composio-managed OAuth is not available for Microsoft Entra ID (bring your own OAuth app).
Brings dedicated quota and custom app branding.

phases.name: Register Application
steps: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as at least an Application Developer.
Enter a meaningful Name for your app.
Under Supported account types, select who can use the application (Single tenant or Multitenant).
Select Register to complete the app registration.
phases.handoff: Record the Application (client) ID from the Overview page.

phases.name: Configure Redirect URIs and Scopes
steps: Copy the redirect URI from your Composio auth config dashboard.
Add the redirect URI to your app registration ensuring it matches protocol and casing requirements.

phases.name: Publisher verification (CPP account + Partner One ID)
steps: Enroll / verify a Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account
Add the Partner One ID to the app registration (Branding & properties)
Ensure the publisher domain matches your verified domain
phases.handoff: Agent drafts the admin-consent request email for enterprise customers in the meantime

phases.name: Partner account verification
steps: Blue verified badge appears on the consent prompt

phases.name: Admin consent in customer tenants (if required)
steps: Send the tenant admin the admin-consent link
Admin approves permissions for the organization

artefacts.title: Microsoft Entra ID App Registration Details
artefacts.body:
Name: ai-agent-client-app
Supported account types: Multitenant or Single tenant
Redirect URI: <Composio callback URL from your auth config>

artefacts.title: Admin consent request email (for customer IT)
artefacts.body:
Subject: Approve <YourApp> in Microsoft Entra ID

Hi <Admin>,

<YourApp> connects to Microsoft 365 on behalf of your users through Composio. Your tenant requires admin approval for apps that request <permissions> or that come from publishers outside your organization.

Permissions requested (delegated): <User.Read, Mail.Read, ...>
Why: <one line per permission>
Publisher: <Company> (Partner One ID <id> / verification in progress)

Admin consent link:
https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant-id>/adminconsent?client_id=<client-id>

Thanks,
<name>

requirements.label: Privacy Policy URL
requirements.when: Required for public production apps requesting user data.

requirements.label: Publisher verification via a verified Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account
requirements.when: For multitenant apps whose users are in other organizations' tenants (otherwise consent may be blocked)

requirements.label: Tenant admin consent
requirements.when: For org-wide (admin-only) permissions, or tenants that restrict user consent to verified publishers

scopes.purpose: Sign in and read user profile

redirectRules.rule: Redirect URIs must begin with the scheme https, with exceptions for some localhost redirect URIs.
Redirect URIs are case-sensitive and must match the case of the URL path of your running application.
HTTPS only (some localhost exceptions); case-sensitive match on the path.

blockers.symptom: Users in a customer tenant see 'Need admin approval' / cannot consent to your app
blockers.cause: Your multitenant app isn't publisher verified and the tenant restricts user consent (risk-based step-up or verified-publishers-only policy), or you requested admin-only permissions.
blockers.fix: Complete publisher verification (CPP account + Partner One ID), request only user-consentable delegated permissions, or ask the tenant admin to grant admin consent.
blockers.fallback: Single-tenant app registration inside each customer's tenant for enterprise pilots.

blockers.symptom: AADSTS50011: The reply URL specified in the request does not match the reply URLs configured for the application
blockers.cause: The redirect URI sent in the login request does not match any configured redirect URIs in the app registration.
blockers.fix: Add the exact redirect URI from your Composio dashboard to the Microsoft Entra app registration.
blockers.fallback: Verify URL encoding and trailing slashes.

blockers.symptom: Access to XMLHttpRequest at login endpoint has been blocked by CORS policy: No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header is present
blockers.cause: Attempting to use the authorization code flow for a Single Page Application without configuring CORS or setting the redirect URI type to spa.
blockers.fix: Update the redirect URI type to spa using the application manifest editor in the Microsoft Entra admin center.
blockers.fallback: Ensure origin header is correctly sent.

checklist.text: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as an Application Developer.
Register a new application and record the Application (client) ID.
Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard auth config.
Add the redirect URI to the application registration respecting HTTPS and case rules.

uncertainties: Exact enterprise review durations and third-party partner verification timelines are not specified in the documentation.
Exact AADSTS error codes shown to blocked users vary by tenant policy; the blocker's symptom text is paraphrased.
Microsoft doesn't publish a timeline for Partner Program account verification; the 1–21 day range is an estimate.
